description: LAG/LEAD with a non-null default still returns nullable when the tracked column itself is nullable, since the tracked column's own NULL values flow through unchanged

columns.name: prev_discount
columns.note: the default only replaces the boundary NULL; discount's own NULLs still pass through LAG

columns.name: next_discount
columns.note: the default only replaces the boundary NULL; discount's own NULLs still pass through LEAD

name: lag_lead_default_with_nullable_source_stays_nullable
query_sql:
-- @name LagLeadDefaultNullableSource
-- @returns :many
SELECT id, discount, LAG(discount, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS prev_discount, LEAD(discount, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS next_discount FROM sales
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE sales (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL, department TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL, discount INTEGER, sale_date DATE NOT NULL)

sqlc_comparison.scythe_improvement: scythe narrows only when both the tracked expression and the default are proven non-null, avoiding an unsound narrowing when the source column can itself be NULL
sqlc_comparison.sqlc_behavior: sqlc does not model the LAG/LEAD default argument and marks the result nullable, matching this case but for the wrong reason
